q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: WITH V1 AS (SELECT bar, beer FROM serves ORDER BY bar), V2 AS (SELECT DISTINCT bar1.bar AS barA, bar2.bar AS barB FROM V1 AS bar1, V1 AS bar2 WHERE bar1.bar > bar2.bar), V3 AS (SELECT barA, barB FROM V2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT beer FROM V1 AS serves_1 WHERE serves_1.bar = barA AND NOT serves_1.beer IN (SELECT beer FROM V1 AS serves_2 WHERE serves_2.bar = barB)) OR EXISTS(SELECT beer FROM V1 AS serves_2 WHERE serves_2.bar = barB AND NOT serves_2.beer IN (SELECT beer FROM V1 AS serves_1 WHERE serves_1.bar = barA))) SELECT * FROM V3

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they use different approaches to identify bars that serve unique beers (i.e., beers not served by any other bar) and bars that serve common beers (i.e., beers served by at least one other bar). Q1 uses a NOT EXISTS subquery to find bars that serve unique beers and another NOT EXISTS subquery to find bars that serve common beers. Q2, on the other hand, uses a CTE (Common Table Expression) to create a virtual table of all beer-bar pairs, then uses another CTE to create a virtual table of unique pairs (i.e., pairs where no other pair has the same beer), and finally uses a WHERE clause to filter out pairs where the beer is not served by any other bar.
